title: Coding with AI episode 3: fixing a real world bug in Redis vector sets with LLMs
summary: Antirez uses Claude to find a segfault introduced by his own refactor of Redis vector sets, stressing that giving the right context makes it work.

assertions.quote: it's very important to provide as fast as possible the right context.

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: so it knows the version of the code when it was correct and the version of the code modified with the bug.

verdicts.note: Localizing bugs from diffs and traces is a known LLM strength, but success depends on the cause being visible in the supplied context.

assertions.quote: it immediately found my bug, which was awesome.

verdicts.note: AI reviewers do catch real defects missed by humans, though with notable false-positive rates; complement, not replacement.

assertions.quote: if I was less experienced at working with LLMs, I could just drop the implementation here

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.
